fair_value_policy: Fair Value V2.1 is the sole valuation baseline. Semantic scores in this file must not directly overwrite official numeric macro series or Fair Value.
summary: Material changes since the morning snapshot: China's August activity data showed industrial output accelerating to 5.2% y/y while retail sales slowed to 0.4% and fixed-asset investment fell 7.2% in January-August, reinforcing a production-versus-demand imbalance. U.S. 10-year Treasury yields traded above 5%, the highest since 2007 in Reuters market reporting, and the dollar index rose to 99.58 as Fed hike pricing exceeded 92%. Reuters also reported that half of Russia's six largest diesel-producing refineries cut or halted output after Ukrainian strikes, while Russia and Ukraine continued energy-infrastructure attacks despite a proposed truce. Middle East oil/shipping risk remains very high.

macro_summary.taiwan_equity_implication: Taiwan equities face a tighter discount-rate and energy-cost environment: U.S. 10Y yields crossed 5%, oil remains above $100, and diesel/refining disruption has broadened from the Gulf to Russia. China's stronger factory output is supportive for regional industrial demand, but very weak retail sales and investment signal poor domestic-demand breadth. Taiwan AI/HPC exports remain the principal offset.
macro_summary.notes: Official numeric series remain authoritative. Reuters market prices/probabilities and semantic scores are research evidence only.

US_PCE_CORE_PCE.latest_official: July 2026: headline PCE +3.7% y/y; core PCE +3.3% y/y.

key_drivers.name: U.S. 10-year yield crosses 5%
key_drivers.observed: Reuters reported the benchmark U.S. 10-year Treasury yield at 5.004% on September 15, the highest since 2007, while Fed hike market pricing exceeded 92%.
key_drivers.interpretation: The higher global discount-rate regime is an immediate valuation headwind for long-duration Taiwan semiconductor and AI-hardware equities even if earnings growth remains strong.

key_drivers.name: China August production improves but demand remains weak
key_drivers.observed: Reuters, citing China's National Bureau of Statistics, reported industrial output +5.2% y/y versus +4.5% in July and 4.8% consensus; retail sales slowed to +0.4% versus 0.8% consensus; January-August fixed-asset investment fell 7.2%.
key_drivers.interpretation: China's manufacturing/technology cycle improved, but weak household demand and investment reduce confidence in a broad domestic recovery. Taiwan upstream industrial exposure gets a mixed signal.

key_drivers.name: Russian refinery damage deepens global diesel constraint
key_drivers.observed: Reuters reported half of Russia's six top diesel-producing refineries significantly reduced or halted output in September after Ukrainian strikes; energy attacks continued despite a proposed truce.
key_drivers.interpretation: A second independent refined-product supply shock increases persistence of diesel, freight and industrial-logistics inflation beyond the Gulf disruption.

key_drivers.name: Middle East energy and shipping shock remains dominant
key_drivers.observed: Brent traded around $107.35 on September 15 as the Saudi East-West pipeline remained offline, Hormuz traffic stayed severely depressed and Houthi attacks broadened Saudi/Red Sea risk.
key_drivers.interpretation: Delivered-energy, freight and marine-insurance stress remains persistent and inflationary.

key_risks: U.S. 10-year yields above 5% can compress Taiwan technology valuation multiples.
Middle East crude/shipping disruption and Russian refinery damage are now simultaneous energy-inflation channels.
China's industrial rebound is not matched by household consumption or investment, limiting breadth of regional demand recovery.
Fed decision on September 16 and Taiwan central-bank decision on September 17 create near-term policy event risk.
VIX, copper and USD/TWD exact values remain stale because no sufficiently authoritative newer exact observation was incorporated.

policy_tone.fed: Hawkish market pricing; no official September decision yet. Reuters reported over 92% market probability of a hike.
policy_tone.taiwan_central_bank: No new decision; September 17 meeting pending. Reuters poll base case remains a 2% hold.
policy_tone.china: August activity data show stronger industrial output but weak consumption/investment, increasing pressure for demand support without implying an announced new policy in this snapshot.
policy_tone.global: Energy-security and refined-product risks remain inflationary and growth-negative.

events.observed_evidence: Saudi-Houthi attacks continue; the East-West pipeline remains offline and Hormuz traffic remains severely depressed.
events.semantic_interpretation: Simultaneous threats to Hormuz, Saudi bypass infrastructure and Red Sea/Bab el-Mandeb keep delivered-energy, freight and insurance risk extremely high.

events.observed_evidence: Reuters reported half of Russia's six top diesel-producing refineries cut or halted output after Ukrainian strikes, while both sides continued energy attacks despite a proposed truce.
events.semantic_interpretation: Russian refinery disruption adds an independent persistent diesel/freight inflation channel to the Gulf shock.
